payload.boundary:
INHERITS the first pass's boundary (evidence/draw_context-1.json, superseded). Two changes.

CHANGE 1 - A NEIGHBOUR RETURNS. RIPGREP is inside the boundary again as the working-tree search provider, spawned as a subprocess: argv in, JSON-Lines events out, exit code. It was cut by the first pass and restored by the owner's correction that tree-search and record-search are TWO JOBS. GIT remains the neighbour for the record and for v1 (branch main). Two providers, one facade, one normalized result shape - which the first pass called duplication and which is in fact fit.

CHANGE 2 - THE MACHINERY ITSELF MOVES INSIDE. engine/machines/compile.ts (the evidence-form builder) and engine/machine.ts (the token model) are now INSIDE the boundary, because Half C changes them: the compiler injects the review rounds at the single source, and the token model gains reopen. The first pass had neither in scope. This is the most consequential boundary change of the rewalk - it means i12 modifies the machinery that runs i12, which is why the trunk/worktree gap keeps biting.

EVERYTHING ELSE INHERITED: engine/deliverable.ts, engine/tools.ts, engine/git.ts, engine/worktree.ts, the lint module, the machine_state ledger nodes, package.json. Outside: git, ripgrep, the machine-local config dir, the ledger, the harness, the owner, the board and phone lane as readers.

THE INTERFACE THAT MATTERS MOST is unchanged in kind but sharper in stakes: between a CHECK and its VERDICT. It now has a second instance - between a METHOD'S REQUIREMENT and THE FORM THAT COLLECTS IT. Both are places where something written must become something asked for, and both were broken in the same way.
payload.intended_use: An agent walking any iteration uses the lane to read, search and edit, receives its rules with its work, and reaches gates that REVIEW THEMSELVES: the gate's own acceptance items, then verify, validate, red-team and a verdict it cannot skip. Where a round finds the work wanting, the verdict is REOPEN and the machine carries it out - re-activating the named states and everything derived from them, marking the first pass superseded so the record shows both. The owner sets their involvement anywhere from adjudicating every gate to being absent, and can afterwards read which checks were computed, which were asserted, and what each round actually found.
payload.excluded_use:
INHERITS the first pass's twelve, with three added by Half C.

- Does NOT index product files. Does NOT do structural/AST matching. Does NOT keep a second search implementation. Does NOT replace se_get_search's BM25. Does NOT write outside the product except se_config into the machine-local dir. Does NOT let a lint judge intent. Does NOT let a lint park a run. Does NOT push, force-push or rewrite history. Does NOT change what the board or phone RENDER. Does NOT fix the trunk/worktree gap. Does NOT touch adjudication policy - killers stay agent-blessable.
- ADDED: does NOT provide an ADVERSARIAL SECOND PARTY for the red-team. The round is written and answered by the same agent. That is weaker than v1's human adjudicator, it is the honest ceiling of this iteration, and building a separate reviewing agent is explicitly out of scope.
- ADDED: does NOT ERASE a superseded fill. A reopen marks; it never deletes. The evidence of a rejected first pass is part of the record, not litter.
- ADDED: does NOT SWEEP every method note against the forms that should collect it. Three such gaps were found by accident today; the systematic sweep is owed work, not this iteration's.
